result:
I split the old catch-all reason of `--bounds` into five reasons, based on how the name was bound, and committed it locally as 41ea2c35 (not pushed; the driver runs the full suite and pushes). The brief's probe shows all five reasons, and the touched tests, both clippy versions (1.97 and CI's 1.99.1) and `pre-push-check.sh` pass.

**What changed:** when the old syntax rules give no specific reason, `bounds_reasons.nika` now takes the first name the site reads and finds how the enclosing function binds it. All of that is in Nikaia; on the Rust side, `bounds_report.rs` only passes the function's parameters and body (and the interner) through the two adapters. The reasons hold no names or lines, so `scripts/proved.nika` already gives one row per kind and needed no change.

**Unproved sites over the tools package** (`lower-std --bounds`, 1,993 in all):

| Count | Reason |
| ---: | :--- |
| 692 | the old catch-all (was 1,862) |
| 582 | a counter a loop changes (#1053 step 4, #432) |
| 379 | a parameter no precondition bounds (ADR-269 D5) |
| 127 | a value read out of a list (#797, #798) |
| 96 | the length of another list (#388) |
| 60 | a call's result (#382) |
| 37 | a list of lists (#385) |
| 7 | an `if` or `match` value (#1053) |
| 6 | a product of two unknowns (#386) |
| 4 | a negation |
| 3 | a field (#384) |

So the next prover extension has a clear first choice: the loop counter (#1053 step 4) covers 582 sites.

**Tests:** the seven `it` modules that use `--bounds` passed (65 tests). No existing test asserts the old catch-all text, so none needed updating, and I added no tests, as the brief said.

**Not mine, left alone:** `lower-std` on the current tree rewrites `crates/nikaia-std/src/tools/lowered/project_members.rs` (`TrustedMap` becomes `HashMap`, 14 lines) without any change of mine. It's still modified in the working tree and not committed; someone should check develop's `lower-std` fixpoint. This is under `Needs:` in the report.

**Disk:** nothing freed; the test cache is 3.6 GB and 17 GB of disk is free. The report lists the large cache entries.
